It is a SHOULD-FIX rather than a MUST-FIX because no claim is falsified: every digest, landing, currency value and register token in the three affected sentences verifies exactly, and the rendered text stays unambiguous.

finalVerdict: OBJECT. Zero MUST-FIX, one SHOULD-FIX. The substance of D-347 is sound and I could not break it. All ten cited digests recompute EXACT against live bytes, including both Stage A reviews of the frozen successor. Both Stage A return shapes are recited exactly and neither is flattened: Claude's ACCEPT with no decision field, four empty lists, three numeric zeroes, no advisories and no observations field, and six named observationsNotFindings objects whose four members are recited in the file's own key order with raisedAndRefuted intact; Codex's ACCEPT with a five-member decision object, four empty lists and three absent fields. Every finding-landing recital re-derives correctly, including all five "unlabeled" claims, which I confirmed by checking that no Codex review entry carries an id field. All six Frozen landings hold and match live D-345 verbatim; all ten "do not record as current" protections are present in both the Status block and the Decision; leftover-design of OBL-FC-OUTFAIL-FX is held open and FC-OUTFAIL.committed-run-preserved is held NOT-AUTHORED. Live authority checks pass: HEAD and last heading D-346, required-now 28 in four places, DR-122 and DR-107 and DR-118 tokens quoted as file 08 carries them, DR-117/DR-131/DR-133 open and unSATISFIED, the no-cell-edit branch correctly split around D-236 and advanced to D-346, Condition 2 at 5 of 32 and Condition 4 at 28 of 28 matching the three preceding entries, and a reversibility list that correctly extends D-346's and restores the D-296 it omitted. 112 leftover-join.vN tokens are all lineage-qualified, no wrap splits a token or a code span, no deictic appears, no platform string appears, and nothing is SATISFIED or QUALIFIED. What fails is terminal punctuation. Three sentence-ending periods are detached from the code spans they close — one orphaned onto the start of line 144 by a wrap, two written with a literal space at lines 176 and 214 — and each renders as a floating period. The register has no instance of either pattern in 21,319 lines, and none of D-343, D-344, D-345 or D-346 has one; D-346's own draft shows the correct handling of the identical construct. Because this text is appended to COORD verbatim on CONSENT, and because CONSENT requires 0 MUST-FIX and 0 SHOULD-FIX, the verdict is OBJECT. Repairing three characters clears it.
